backlog.spec: The guided restarts currently jitter the best centres with a fixed normal sd of 0.03. Replace the constant by a per-restart draw from the seed rng: sigma = exp(rng.uniform(log(0.004), log(0.08))). Pass sigma into _solve_once and use it in rng.normal(0, sigma, (n, 2)). Nothing else changes. Small sigmas refine the same contact graph, large ones jump to neighbouring basins; mixing scales removes the need to tune one value.
backlog.title: Log-uniform jitter scale for guided restarts

backlog.spec: Replace the guided-restart branch in solve with a basin-hopping move used for the whole second half of the time budget. Let _solve_once accept full initial centres and radii without adding its own noise. A move: copy the best centres, pick the 1 to 3 circles with the smallest radii (or random ones with probability 0.3), and move each to the location of the largest empty hole, estimated by sampling 2000 rng points in the square and choosing the one maximising min(distance to walls, min over other circles of distance to centre minus radius); add Gaussian noise of sd 0.01 to all other centres; start radii at 0.9 times their current values and the relocated ones at the hole size. Run SLSQP from there, repair, and accept if the sum of radii improves on the best. Keep pure random restarts for the first half.
backlog.title: Basin hopping: perturb the best packing by relocating the smallest circles

backlog.spec: Track the number of consecutive guided restarts that failed to improve the best sum of radii. In the second half of the budget, set the probability of a guided restart to 0.8 while that counter is below 8, and to 0.2 once it reaches 8 (reset the counter to 0 whenever best improves, whether through a guided or a random restart). All randomness stays on the seed rng. This spends more time on exploitation while it pays, and returns to exploration when the incumbent basin is exhausted.
backlog.title: Stagnation fallback from guided to random restarts

backlog.spec: Tune the settings rather than the algorithm: set MAX_ITER to 500 and pass ftol=1e-10 in the SLSQP options so restarts are not cut off before the active set settles (the default ftol 1e-6 stops with radii still about 1e-4 short per run). To keep the deadline safe, track the longest restart duration so far and stop the restart loop when the elapsed CPU time plus 1.5 times that duration would exceed 0.9 * time_limit, replacing the fixed TIME_FRACTION test; raise TIME_FRACTION to 0.9 accordingly. In guided restarts also reduce the perturbation sd from 0.03 to 0.01 and start from the best radii multiplied by 0.95 instead of the constant INIT_RADIUS.
backlog.title: Tighter SLSQP convergence and safer time budget

backlog.spec: Before SLSQP in _solve_once, run a cheap vectorised penalty relaxation to get a much better starting point. Minimise f(c, r) = -sum(r) + mu * (sum over pairs of max(0, r_i + r_j - dist_ij)^2 + sum over circles and walls of max(0, r - wall_distance)^2) with scipy L-BFGS-B and an analytic gradient, bounds 0 <= c <= 1 and 0 <= r <= 0.5, for three stages mu = 10, 100, 1000 with about 150 iterations each, warm-starting each stage from the previous. Feed the result (radii multiplied by 0.98) as x0 to the existing SLSQP call. The penalty stage costs O(n^2) per evaluation with no QP solve, so it is far cheaper than SLSQP iterations and lets SLSQP converge in fewer steps from an almost feasible, well-spread configuration.
backlog.title: Penalty-method L-BFGS pre-relaxation before SLSQP

backlog.spec: Remove the n constraints r >= 0 from the cons vector and instead pass bounds to minimize: centres in [0, 1] and radii in [0, 0.5] (bounds=[(0, 1)] * (2 * n) + [(0, 0.5)] * n). Keep the 4n wall constraints c - r >= 0 and 1 - c - r >= 0 and the pairwise constraints. This shrinks the constraint Jacobian slightly, keeps iterates inside the square (so the np.clip in solve becomes a no-op), and lets each restart finish faster so more restarts fit in the budget.
backlog.title: Move box and positivity constraints into SLSQP bounds

backlog.spec: Split the 0.8 * time_limit budget into two equal episodes. Each episode runs the current scheme on its own: random restarts for the first half of the episode, then the 50/50 guided/random mix from that episode's own best for the second half. The episode best is reset at the start of the second episode; solve returns the better of the two episode bests. This hedges against the first episode locking onto a poor basin, which is the main source of seed-to-seed variance.
backlog.title: Two independent half-budget episodes

backlog.spec: In _solve_once, supply exact gradients so SLSQP stops spending its time on finite differences. Pass jac for the objective (a constant vector: zeros for the 2n centre entries, -1 for the n radius entries) and add a 'jac' entry to the constraint dict returning the dense Jacobian of cons with rows in the same order as cons: for each pair (i,j) the derivative of dist - r_i - r_j is (c_i-c_j)/dist w.r.t. c_i, the negative w.r.t. c_j, and -1 for r_i and r_j (guard dist with max(dist,1e-12)); then the four wall blocks (+-1 on the coordinate, -1 on the radius) and the identity for r >= 0. Build the constant wall/radius part once outside the closure. Keep everything else unchanged. Expected effect: each restart becomes many times faster, so far more restarts fit in the same time budget.
backlog.title: Analytic Jacobians for SLSQP

backlog.spec: The best packings with free radii mix large and small circles, but every start uses identical radii of 0.05. In _solve_once, for unguided starts draw initial radii from rng: with probability 0.5 uniform in [0.03, 0.11], otherwise a bimodal draw where k circles (k uniform in 2..8) get radius about 0.04 and the rest about 0.095. Then place centres sequentially by best-of-30 candidate sampling: for each circle in descending radius order, sample 30 rng points inside [r, 1-r]^2 and keep the one with the largest clearance to already placed circles. Finally scale all radii by 0.8 so the start is nearly feasible, and pass it to SLSQP as before.
backlog.title: Non-uniform initial radii and size-diverse starts

backlog.spec: Replace the body of _repair with an exact linear programme: for fixed centres c, maximise sum(r) subject to r_i + r_j <= dist_ij - 2e-10 for all pairs, r_i <= min(x_i, y_i, 1-x_i, 1-y_i) - 1e-10 via bounds, and r_i >= 0, using scipy.optimize.linprog(method='highs'). Then run the existing greedy shrink loop on the LP result as a safety net (and fall back to the old shrink on LP failure), and keep the final subtraction of SHRINK. This gives the best possible radii for the centres instead of a lossy pairwise shrink, and guarantees validity. To keep it cheap, only pairs with dist_ij < 0.5 need to be included in the LP, but the safety shrink must check all pairs.
backlog.title: Final LP radius re-optimisation instead of shrink-only repair
